name: DNA code A4GC(18,10)
description: Find as many DNA words of length 18 as possible, that is, strings over the letters A, C, G, T, such that all words have the same number of letters in {C, G} (that number is free) and any two different words differ in at least 10 positions.
contract: construct() -> list of distinct strings of length 18 over the capital letters A, C, G, T (at least one word and at most 20000; a longer list is invalid). Score: number of words, maximized.
notes: Lower bound 920 (construction 'l'), not proven optimal; the table was last updated 23 June 2010. The tables list the maximum over the GC-content w (the same number of letters from C and G in every word); this task lets the code choose any one w, so a table value is reachable whichever w it uses (until 2026-11-18 the task fixed w = floor(n/2), which put four records of Aboluion et al. out of reach).
Entry A4GC(18,10) of the Gaborit-King table of lower bounds for DNA codes of length 18, GC-content 9 and minimum Hamming distance 10.

The table dates from 2010. A 2026 repository of later codes has none for these parameters, and the tables of Montemanni, Smith and Koul (2014), which list the best values known then, show no larger one. Papers published after 2014 were not searched systematically.
Only open entries with a bound of at most 2000 words in the table are tasks, so that the pairwise check stays cheap.

science_relevance.reason: The four papers have the size of DNA codes with constant GC-content and a minimum Hamming distance as their main objective and are the sources of the lower bounds in the Gaborit-King table that the task instance comes from; the evaluator checks exactly the code definition of King (2003).
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a DNA code of length 18 (words over A, C, G, T with exactly floor(18/2) letters from C and G, pairwise Hamming distance at least 10) with as many words as possible.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Such word sets serve as barcodes, microarray probes and tags in DNA computing and storage, where words must not hybridise with each other; a constant GC-content gives similar melting temperatures and a large Hamming distance makes mismatched pairing unlikely. The maximum size is unknown for almost all parameters and the pinned table has been the reference for lower bounds since 2010, so a larger code is a new lower bound.

papers.title: Bounds for DNA Codes with Constant GC-Content
papers.task_relation: The paper defines the quantity the task maximises for length 18 and distance 10 (GC-content floor(18/2)); its lexicographic constructions and Johnson-type bounds underlie the table the task starts from. The task covers the plain constant-GC variant.
papers.primary_goal: Derive upper and lower bounds on the maximum size of DNA codes with constant GC-content and minimum Hamming distance, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, and construct larger codes than previously published.

papers.title: Linear constructions for DNA codes
papers.task_relation: Its constructions give many entries of the table for length 18 and distance 10 (superscripts c, l and m on the pinned page); the task asks to beat the tabulated size. Covers the plain constant-GC variant.
papers.primary_goal: Construct DNA codes with constant GC-content from linear and related codes and tabulate the resulting lower bounds.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Constant GC-Content DNA Codes
papers.task_relation: Supplies table entries marked a, b and colon-optimal on the pinned page; the task asks for a larger code than the tabulated one for length 18, distance 10.
papers.primary_goal: Improve the lower bounds on the size of constant GC-content DNA codes, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, by stochastic local search, and prove some entries optimal by clique computations.

papers.title: Construction of Constant GC-Content DNA Codes via a Variable Neighbourhood Search Algorithm
papers.task_relation: Supplies the many table entries marked v on the pinned page; the task asks for a larger code for length 18, distance 10.
papers.primary_goal: Construct large constant GC-content DNA codes with a variable neighbourhood search algorithm.
